findings.detail: The criterion requires the three specific entries (8625-7bea-67db-4cdc, 9305-b42c-3262-4c58, e27c-5a20-cd13-43b2) to reach `done` state on the live store. The ticket's own attestation (in the AC3 text and Phase 2 comment) explicitly acknowledges this has NOT happened: 'the store holds 898 pending entries and these sit at sorted indices 458 / 499 / 786 behind a batch cap of 5. That starvation is a separate defect.' The attestation confirms the fix removes the blocking reason (live enrich() calls succeed in ~8s), but does not attest that the entries have actually reached `done`. The criterion's own text says 'Evidence is live-store drain progress, outside any code snapshot' — and no such evidence of `done` state is recorded in the ticket snapshot. The Phase 2 comment explicitly marks AC3 as unchecked ('[ ] AC3 — see the note below on the three entries') and states 'the fix removes the reason those entries could not complete, but it does not by itself make them reach `done` on this store.'
findings.remediation: Record a ticket comment with evidence that the three entries (8625-7bea-67db-4cdc, 9305-b42c-3262-4c58, e27c-5a20-cd13-43b2) have reached `done` state on the live store — naming the observed queue state (e.g. from `rebar enrich status` output or a store inspection), the timestamp when each reached `done`, and the principal/environment that observed it.

data.remediation: How to resolve the unmet criteria: use the evidence path that matches each one. For codebase-verifiable work, complete any unfinished work and make its proof discoverable in the repository. For evidence that inherently lives outside the repository, mark the criterion with the exact `[non-codebase]` tag and add a comment to this ticket that documents the concrete artifacts that meet it (commands and their output, links, or the reasoning that ties the evidence to the criterion). The completion verifier reads this ticket's comments, so properly tagged evidence you record there is taken into account on the next verification. An untagged external criterion cannot be satisfied by a ticket comment alone. Then re-verify. Note that a finding reporting a ticket record as absent means it was NOT VISIBLE IN THE TICKET SNAPSHOT THE VERIFIER READ — that snapshot is pinned when the run starts, so a record written after the pin, or not yet committed to the store, reads as missing even though it exists; re-verify after the write lands rather than re-recording evidence you already wrote.
